sentence: The NHS says metronidazole is an antibiotic used for bacterial infections, including skin infections, mouth infections, bacterial vaginosis and pelvic inflammatory disease, and is available only on prescription.
note: NHS About metronidazole: antibiotic for bacterial infections incl. skin infections, rosacea, mouth and dental infections, bacterial vaginosis, pelvic inflammatory disease; prescription only.

sentence: MedlinePlus says tinidazole treats trichomoniasis, bacterial vaginosis, giardiasis and amoebiasis, and describes it as a nitroimidazole antimicrobial.
note: MedlinePlus tinidazole page: treats trichomoniasis, bacterial vaginosis, giardiasis, amebiasis; class nitroimidazole antimicrobials.

sentence: A therapeutic review says metronidazole has a limited spectrum that covers various protozoa and most anaerobic bacteria, and that it lacks efficacy against aerobic organisms.
note: PubMed 9360057 'Metronidazole. A therapeutic review and update': limited spectrum covering various protozoans and most Gram-negative and Gram-positive anaerobes; no efficacy against aerobes. PMID 363399 (Brogden 1978) abstract does not carry the aerobe wording, so the first-pass URL was wrong. [second-pass edit]

sentence: A review of tinidazole describes it as active in the laboratory against most clinically important anaerobic bacteria.
note: PubMed 6749473 (tinidazole review): like metronidazole, active in vitro against most clinically important obligate anaerobes.

sentence: The NHS lists feeling or being sick, diarrhoea and a slight metallic taste in the mouth as common side effects of metronidazole.
note: NHS side effects of metronidazole: common ones are feeling or being sick, diarrhoea, slight metallic taste.

sentence: MedlinePlus lists a sharp, unpleasant metallic taste among the side effects of tinidazole.
note: Returned MedlinePlus text confirmed only a sharp, unpleasant metallic taste; nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite appeared only in a patent, not MedlinePlus, so the rest is unverified. [second-pass edit]

sentence: The NHS lists yellowing of the skin or whites of the eyes among the rare but serious side effects of metronidazole.
note: NHS lists yellowing of skin or eyes among warning signs of rare serious side effects (under 1 in 1,000). The 'liver or gallbladder problems' interpretation and a care route for metronidazole were not in the returned text (the GP/111 route came from the doxazosin page). [second-pass edit]

sentence: MedlinePlus advises avoiding alcohol and products containing alcohol during tinidazole treatment and for a period afterwards, as they may cause an upset stomach, vomiting, stomach cramps, headaches, sweating and flushing.
note: MedlinePlus tinidazole: do not drink alcohol or use alcohol-containing products during treatment and for 3 days after; may cause upset stomach, vomiting, stomach cramps, headaches, sweating, flushing. Number of days correctly omitted.

sentence: A review of alcohol and antibiotic interactions says the concern about alcohol with tinidazole rests on its chemical similarity to metronidazole, with no direct data identified.
note: PMC7038249 review (snippets only): tinidazole entries are inconsistent (one says avoid alcohol 72 h, another says alcohol may be consumed); one notes a potential concern due to chemical similarity to metronidazole with no direct data. 'Labelling' and 'review found no data' attribution not clearly confirmed. [second-pass edit]

sentence: MedlinePlus advises telling the doctor about kidney or liver disease before using metronidazole.
note: MedlinePlus metronidazole: precautions list kidney or liver disease among conditions to tell the doctor about.
